He owns the house we currently live in, his (separated) wife's house, and a bar that has 2 apartments above it. As of now, his wife's house would remain her's or if she passes, go to their 3 children. The house we live in now, would be split amongst the 4 of us. The bar and the apartments would go solely to me. My mom is worried she won't get anything when he does pass away, so she constantly asks if I'll give her half of the bar. I personally want nothing to do with the bar due it being a cause for my parent's alcoholism. My mom says I should just give it all to her if that's the case. I would ask her to at least buy out my half, but she has been mentally abusive to me for most of my life, and constantly sabotaged anything I've done to try and better my own life. I've recently thought about just selling my quarter of the house to my siblings, and the entire bar to them or anyone else who wants it. WIBTA if I decided to leave my mom out of anything I get from my dad's will?

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: I think the answer is 0, meaning you would not be the asshole (YTA) in this scenario. Here's why: 1. **Your dad's will, your decision**: The bar and apartments are being left to you, and it's your decision what to do with them. You have the right to sell or manage them as you see fit. 2. **No obligation to give to your mom**: While your mom may be worried about her financial situation, there's no obligation for you to give her the bar or any part of your inheritance. Your dad's will has already made provisions for her, and she has a separate house that would remain hers. 3. **Your mom's behavior**: Given your mom's history of mental abuse and sabotage, it's understandable that you wouldn't want to give her the bar or any part of your inheritance. You have the right to prioritize your own well-being and protect yourself from toxic relationships. 4. **Selling to siblings or others**: If you decide to sell your quarter of the house or the entire bar, it's your decision who you sell to. If you choose to sell to your siblings or someone else, that's your prerogative. Overall, it seems like you're making a decision that prioritizes your own well-being and financial security, while also considering the complexities of your family dynamics.
